interpretation: The method repairs two different losses rather than treating them as one tail problem. A single Dirichlet polynomial cannot simultaneously remain long enough to majorize log |ζ| accurately and short enough to support the high moments demanded by Markov reconstruction. Splitting A into pieces expected to contribute increasingly little allocates smaller admissible powers to the later, longer pieces; exponentiation then turns the additive split into a product whose factors can be truncated separately when controlled. If a piece is oversized, that point is handled with a shorter majorant plus a small-measure estimate. Working on the exponential moment itself preserves the target upper-bound quantity instead of discarding information into a tail estimate. The gain is multiscale compatibility; the remaining burden is to justify every truncation, bad-point measure, and product integral, and the construction yields only an upper bound.
